title: Thoracic segmental sagittal ROM T1/2-T12/L1 (passive supine CT, patients)
condition: patients without thoracic disease, supine, passive maximal flexion to maximal extension

quantity.name: segmental flexion-extension ROM
quantity.definition: segmental kyphotic angle at maximal flexion minus at maximal extension (superior-endplate Cobb method)

source.authors: Morita D, Yukawa Y, Nakashima H, Ito K, Yoshida G, Machino M, Kanbara S, Iwase T, Kato F
source.sample: 50 patients (34 M, 16 F); 50 patients with cervical or lumbar spinal disease (no thoracic disease or compression fracture) imaged after myelography

protocol.summary: Supine CT in passive maximal flexion and extension; segmental and total T1-L1 ROM.
how_to_use: Distribute a thoracic sagittal motion over T1-L1 in proportion to these segmental ROMs (minimum at T4-T5, rising caudally to T12-L1; T1-T2 also mobile).
Treat as relative distribution only: supine passive ROM (31.7 deg) is much smaller than standing flexion-extension ROM (~58-70 deg) and the sample is older patients.
Flexion and extension are not separated here (ROM = flexion minus extension kyphosis); use the kyphosis test for the two end positions.

measurement.device: 64-row MDCT (GE LightSpeed VCT), 1 mm slices; Cobb-type segmental angles from superior endplates (T1/2-T12/L1)
measurement.posture: supine on triangular pillows (flexion: under upper and lower back; extension: under mid-back and buttocks)
measurement.task: passive maximal flexion and maximal extension

extraction.check_notes: Re-read Table 1 and abstract; cross-checked against differences of digitised Fig 3 flexion/extension angles (all within 0.1 deg).

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
